newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Steel group UGB to sell Fafer - paper.
newsitem.headline: Steel group UGB to sell Fafer - paper.

text.p: Belgian steel group Usines Gustave Boel (UGB), which recently signed a 50/50 cooperation deal with Dutch Hoogovens, is considering selling its Fabrique de Fer (Fafer), Belgian paper Le Soir said on Friday.
The paper said political, economic and union sources had been told of the plan.

Bourse-listed Fafer was being sold because its current size meant its long-term future could not be guaranteed and because of a lack of interest in Fafer from the younger generation of the Boel family which holds 50.5 percent of Fafer.

Belgian radio said Fafer, a major stainless steel producer, was the only steel maker in the Walloon region still hiring new staff. Annual production stands at some 200,000 tonnes, sales at about 15 billion francs.
Le Soir said possible buyers included British Steel, Belgian-Luxembourg group Arbed/Sidmar and France's Usinor-Sacilor.
Analysts recently said shares in Fafer and its shareholder Belgian holding company Henex -- part of the Boel family- controlled Boel Group -- were undervalued and should be bought.

Henex was trading at too large a discount to its intrinsic value as were two of its main interests -- holding company Sofina and Fafer, they said, forecasting an improvement in steel prices and volumes at Fafer.
They said that relative to its intrinsic value Fafer was undervalued by some 30 percent. They also said speculation Hoogovens might buy Fafer was another reason to buy Henex stock.
Henex owns over 22 percent in Fafer, while Fafer has 4.5 percent of Henex. Henex was split off from Fafer in 1981.

In April Fafer said net profit in the six months to December 21, 1996 fell to 111 million Belgian francs from 250 million as a result of disappointing macro-economic growth. It said at the time it expected little improvement in the second half.

In the wake of the collapse of Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq early this year there were efforts on the part of the Walloon regional government to form a single Walloon steel group between Fafer, Clabecq and Cockerill Sambre.
The various parties failed to agree, however.
Clabecq is now in the process of being part-sold to Italian-Swiss group Duferco.
